death.attack.contagion.infection.player: %1$s succumbed to the infection while fighting %2$s
contagion.lore.syringe.1: Use on someone to draw blood
contagion.lore.thermometer.2: Use on someone to take theirs
contagion.lore.sample.use1: Use on a Microscope to analyze
contagion.lore.sample.use2: Use with a Petri Dish to grow a culture
contagion.lore.sample.use3: Sneak + use on someone to transfuse
contagion.lore.culture.use: Off-hand it to test a serum on a Microscope
contagion.lore.prepared: Can be mixed into a serum
contagion.lore.serum.sealed_use1: Use twice to inject yourself, or use on someone
contagion.lore.serum.sealed_use2: Or test it on a culture with a Microscope
contagion.lore.serum.unsealed_use1: Reagent in off-hand + use to add it
contagion.strain.name: Strain %1$s "%2$s %3$s"
contagion.symptom.bleed2: You're bleeding and it won't stop.
contagion.stage.mild_neurological: A dull headache settles behind your eyes.
contagion.stage.mild_hemorrhagic: You notice bruises you don't remember getting.
contagion.stage.moderate: You feel properly sick now. This isn't going away on its own.
contagion.stage.severe: Something is very wrong. Your body is starting to fail.
contagion.stage.terminal: You can feel your life slipping away...
contagion.stage.relief_fading: The relief is fading. The symptoms are coming back.
contagion.hint.syringe: Use the syringe on someone to draw their blood, or sneak + use to draw your own.
contagion.hint.drew_blood: You draw a blood sample from %s.
contagion.hint.drew_own: You draw a sample of your own blood.
contagion.hint.vein_recovering: %s's veins need to recover first (about %s min).
contagion.hint.too_weak: You're too weak to draw blood safely.
contagion.hint.confirm_inject: Inject yourself with this serum? Use again to confirm.
contagion.hint.sealed_serum: Sealed serum: %s. Use twice to inject yourself.
contagion.hint.dish_need_sample: Hold a blood sample in your off-hand to start a culture.
contagion.hint.inoculated: You smear %s's blood on the dish. It needs about %s minutes to grow.
contagion.hint.culture_ready: Colonies have grown. Test a serum on it with a Microscope.
contagion.hint.mortar_need_reagent: Hold a reagent in your off-hand to grind it.
contagion.hint.mortar_only_raw: Only raw reagents can be ground.
contagion.hint.vial_need_reagent: Hold a reagent in your off-hand to add it to the vial.
contagion.hint.mixture_need_reagent: Hold a reagent in your off-hand to add it, or sneak + use to seal the mixture.
contagion.hint.mixture_full: The vial is full. Sneak + use to seal it.
contagion.hint.sealed: Serum sealed. Test it on a culture, or inject it... at your own risk.
contagion.microscope.start_analysis: You prepare a slide of %s's blood. Analysis will take about %s seconds.
contagion.microscope.start_culture: You expose %s's culture to the serum. Check back in about %s seconds.
contagion.microscope.seal_first: Seal the serum first (sneak + use) before testing it.
contagion.microscope.need_culture: To test this serum, hold a grown culture (Petri Dish) in your off-hand.
contagion.microscope.culture_growing: That culture hasn't finished growing yet.
contagion.microscope.culture_sterile: Nothing grew in that dish. There's nothing to test on.
contagion.microscope.help: Microscope: use with a blood sample to analyze it, or with a sealed serum (grown culture in off-hand) to test the serum.
contagion.microscope.done_notify: The microscope has finished. Use it to read the result.
contagion.microscope.degraded: The sample has degraded too much to read. Blood keeps about %s days.
contagion.microscope.antibodies: Antibodies against the pathogen found. The donor is immune.
contagion.microscope.negative_note: (Very early infections can be missed. If in doubt, test again later.)
contagion.microscope.identified2: It looks like it takes a combination of three active compounds to neutralize it.
contagion.microscope.nothing_new_donor: Nothing new compared to the last slide of %s's blood from that day. Try a fresh sample tomorrow, or another donor.
contagion.microscope.no_insight: No new insights from this slide. A sicker donor gives clearer results.
contagion.culture.efficacy.0: No effect. The culture keeps growing.
contagion.culture.efficacy.2: Growth strongly inhibited, but the culture survives.
contagion.culture.trace: There's a faint, unusual reaction at the edges of the dish...
contagion.culture.tissue.1: Healthy tissue sample: noticeable cell damage.
contagion.fact.category: The pathogen's membrane breaks down when exposed to %s compounds. One active agent is probably of that kind.
contagion.fact.form: The %s active agent only works when %s.
contagion.fact.toxic: %s destroyed healthy cells in the sample. It is probably toxic to patients.
contagion.fact.inert: %s showed no interaction with the pathogen at all.
contagion.log.result.positive_insight: POSITIVE (%s viral load); new insight recorded
contagion.inject.cured: Within minutes the fever breaks. You can feel your body fighting the infection off. You are cured, and you won't catch it again.
contagion.inject.relief_clear: The symptoms ease noticeably. It's working... partly.
contagion.inject.relief_faint: Maybe you feel a tiny bit better. Hard to tell.
contagion.inject.weaker: The relief feels weaker than last time.
contagion.inject.healthy: You don't feel anything in particular.
contagion.inject.toxic1: Your stomach turns. Something in that serum didn't agree with you.
contagion.inject.toxic2: Your veins burn. That was a bad idea.
contagion.title.cured_sub: The infection is gone. You are immune.
contagion.transfuse.antibodies: You feel a little stronger. Something in that blood is fighting for you.
contagion.beaker.need_water: Fill the beaker with water first (water bottle or bucket).
contagion.beaker.need_reagent: Use a reagent on the beaker to boil it.
contagion.beaker.need_heat: The water needs heat below the beaker: campfire, fire, lava or a magma block.
contagion.beaker.need_vial: Use an Empty Vial to collect the extract.
contagion.book.title: Research Journal
contagion.book.author: the survivors
contagion.book.manual.blood.1: Use a Syringe on someone (sneak + use: yourself), then use the sample on a Microscope.
contagion.book.manual.tips.1: Early infections can test negative. Sicker donors give clearer results.
contagion.book.manual.tips.2: One new fact per donor per day. Veins need hours to recover between draws.
contagion.book.manual.cultures.1: Petri Dish in hand, blood in off-hand: use. It takes time to grow.
contagion.book.manual.cultures.2: Only blood with enough pathogen grows. Cultures die after a while.
contagion.book.manual.preparing.1: Mortar in hand, reagent in off-hand: grind it.
contagion.book.manual.preparing.2: Beaker: water, heat below, then a reagent. Collect the extract with an Empty Vial.
contagion.book.manual.mixing.1: Empty Vial in hand, reagent in off-hand: use. Up to 4. Raw, ground or extract.
contagion.book.manual.testing.1: Sealed serum in hand, grown culture in off-hand: use on a Microscope.
contagion.book.manual.testing.2: Safe but slow. Watch for odd reactions: preparation matters.
contagion.book.manual.treating.1: Use a sealed serum twice to inject yourself, or use it on someone.
contagion.book.manual.other.2: Face Mask: wear it to slow the spread.
contagion.book.manual.other.3: Sneak + use a Blood Sample on someone to transfuse it.
contagion.journal.chat_open: Use without sneaking to open the full journal.
contagion.command.released: The pathogen has been released (%s new host(s)).
contagion.command.nobody: There is nobody left to infect.
contagion.command.outbreak: Somewhere among you, patient zero has been infected. Nobody knows who.
contagion.command.tip: Tip: craft a Research Journal (book + paper + coal). It has a lab manual and tracks your research.
contagion.command.no_strain: No strain exists yet. It is created at the first infection.
contagion.command.mutated: The pathogen mutated into %s. All research is obsolete.

advancements.contagion.alchemist.title: Kitchen Chemistry
advancements.contagion.alchemist.descrip: Boil a reagent into an extract
